title: throughput-pulse-latency-econ-field-scan
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational-first sketch comparing two serving heuristics under realistic customer mixes: (A) steady-slot reservation (baseline) and (B) throughput-pulse (short-duration burst pooling). Goal is to summarize p50/p90/p99, cost per 1k queries, and qualitative burst behavior so product/SDR/solutions teams have a tight narrative for customer conversations.

Scope and test setup:
- Workload: mixed chat (60%), short-completion assistant (30%), embeddings/batch (10%).
- Models/profiles tested: r-instruct-13B-fp16, r-instruct-13B-int8, r-chat-70B-q4 (approx config names).
- Hardware: A100-80GB equivalent (profiled), scheduler was identical except admission policy.
- Session mix: steady (flat 100 qps sustained), microburst (base 20 qps, 10s bursts to 120 qps every 60s), random spikes (poisson lambda tuned).
- Key knobs: batching window 5ms vs 20ms, KV cache enabled vs disabled, slot reservation 4-slab vs dynamic pulse pooling.

Topline summary (quick read):
- Throughput-pulse reduces amortized cost in microburst scenarios by ~18–27% vs steady reservation for mixed chat workloads (best gains on int8).
- P99 tail improves on steady reservation for short bursts when batching window is lowered to 5ms; however, p50/p90 trade slightly worse for high quant modes when KV cache miss rate rises.
- Latency-cost sweet spot for most customers: int8 + throughput-pulse + 5ms batching + aggressive KV prefetch => ~15% cost reduction with neutral p95.
- Larger models (q4 70B) see smaller relative savings (6–10%) because decode CPU/GPU constraints dominate over slot amortization.

ASCII charts (interpretation-first):
1) p95 vs cost per 1k requests (steady vs pulse) (lower is better):
   Steady  : p95 110ms | cost $3.40 /1k   [######--------]
   Pulse   : p95 105ms | cost $2.75 /1k   [#########-----]
   (bars are relative weight of dollar cost)

2) Burst response timeline (microburst 0-60s, single burst at t=10s):
   Time (s):  0    5   10   15   20   30   40   50   60
   Steady p95 (ms): 100  102 140 120 110 105 103 102 100
   Pulse  p95 (ms): 100  115 118 110 108 105 103 102 100
   Note: pulse shows higher jitter immediately pre-burst but lower peak at t=10 due to pooled slots freeing capacity.

Detailed numbers (selected slices):
- Mixed chat, r-instruct-13B-int8:
  - Steady (100 qps sustained): p50=48ms, p90=94ms, p95=110ms, p99=220ms, cost=$3.10/1k
  - Pulse (base 20 qps, 10s bursts): p50=52ms, p90=98ms, p95=105ms, p99=165ms, cost=$2.38/1k
- Mixed chat, r-instruct-13B-fp16:
  - Steady: p50=44ms, p90=88ms, p95=108ms, p99=270ms, cost=$3.65/1k
  - Pulse: p50=48ms, p90=92ms, p95=104ms, p99=190ms, cost=$3.00/1k
- r-chat-70B-q4 (heavy decode):
  - Steady: p95=280ms, p99=520ms, cost=$9.50/1k
  - Pulse: p95=270ms, p99=480ms, cost=$8.85/1k

Why numbers differ (notes):
- Cost delta driven mostly by amortized slot utilization during burst windows. Pulse pools short-lived slots across tenants to increase packing efficiency; this reduces idle GPU cycles billed to reserved pools.
- p99 improvement for pulse in mixed chat often comes from reduced queueing at admission layer (fast preemptive allocation), but can regress if KV cache cold-starts happen simultaneously across many sessions.
- Quantization interacts with batching: int8's smaller memory footprint increases effective packing so pulse gains amplify. q4 models are bottlenecked on decoder throughput so slot packing adds limited benefit.

Tradeoffs observed:
- Developer UX: pulse requires more observability (per-request admission logs) to debug rare p99 events.
- Predictability: steady reservation is simpler for SLAs; pulse slightly increases jitter but lowers worst-case monetary exposure.
- Cost accounting: per-tenant attribution for pooled slots more complex (need amortization model).

Operational checklist (for next-run):
- Re-run with (a) higher KV prefetch threshold, (b) alternative admission pacing (leaky-bucket smoothing), (c) more realistic multi-tenant interference (N=200).
- Add per-token energy telemetry to correlate decode-bound runs with lesser slot packing gains.
- Sanity: run long 24h steady vs pulse comparison to check for seasonal artifacts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: How sensitive are pulse savings to different burst cadence patterns (e.g., 5s bursts every 30s vs 10s every 60s)? ACTION: simulate 4 cadence variants.
- Q: How to price pooled-slot amortization for Dedicated customers? Need finance + legal input. OWNER: Priya.
- TODO: Wire up session-level admission trace to the console (trace id mapping). OWNER: Ethan.
- NOTE TO SELF: follow up on GPU kernel scheduling optimization branch in PR #984 — latency interplay with pulse not fully traced.

Recommendations (draft for PM/CS one-pager):
- For most SaaS customers with bursty UX patterns (chat widgets, search assistants): recommend int8 + throughput-pulse as default profile; highlight ~15–25% cost upside and neutral p95.
- For heavy decode enterprise workloads (70B class): conservative approach: keep steady reservation for strict SLA customers but offer pulse as elective cost-savings pilot with observability hook.
- Product ask: add pulse-mode toggle in rollout UI + simulated cost preview for a 30-day window.

Appendix A — quick math (amortization nugget):
- Example: steady reserves 4 slots at $X/hr each → billed even when idle. Pulse allows these slots to be reused by short-lived sessions during bursts, increasing utilization from 18% -> 43% in our traces, translating to roughly 40% less idle time charged per useful query. Net effect after kernel inefficiencies was an 18–27% reduction in per-query cost.

Appendix B — quick experiment notes (raw):
- Script used: /bench/run_pulse_scan.sh (local repo, see PR 984).
- Fidelity: 3 independent runs per cell, 95% CI reported above.
- Artifacts: CSVs uploaded to GCS under gs://redwood-bench/pulse-scan/2029-07-18/*

- confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-DEVOPS-PULSE-OVERVIEW (internal)

Rough executive blurb (for a one slide summary):
Throughput-pulse = a low-friction optimization for bursty apps: 15% median cost savings, p95 parity in most cases, and improved p99 in mixed chat due to faster admission. Recommend a beta for Dedicated customers with telemetry hook and an opt-in console toggle.

Work items for shipping collateral:
- Create a short 1-pager (customer-facing) with two charts (cost delta, burst timeline). OWNER: Sofia. DUE: 2029-07-29
- Console: add simulated 30-day cost preview for pulse. OWNER: Product-Console team.
- Finance: propose amortization model and default billing FAQ. OWNER: Priya.

Unresolved / risks:
- Multi-tenant fairness: pulse pooling could increase tail for a small subset of tenants during large simultaneous bursts; mitigation needs preemption rules.
- Legal: contract language for pooled capacity for Dedicated customers.

End of sketch.
